Moving away. My impression early on was that moving is tough, and being the new kid means being bullied and ostracized and all sorts of things. What I came to discover was that it's no walk in the part, but it's not like the movies either.

The first time or two, it's easy to move away. At least, based on my experience. You assume that it's just bad luck or whatever, and you resolve to make the best of it, and you might actually see it as a new adventure, new experiences.

But now, as an upperclassman in high school who moved for the 7th or 8th time a couple months ago, I feel empty about it all. As a child I didn't make friend easily (teachers would have "talks" with me, to try and help me and stuff) but I managed. I think the more I moved, the more I tried to "replant my roots" and make new friends, because I was convinced each time that it would be the last time I would have to leave, but sure enough, I'd say goodbye to people I knew for a year, give or take, and start all over again in a new place.

This most recent move was the worst yet. I was going to be a drum major, and I'd really grown to like my school's marching band, but just before auditions, we packed up and moved across the state. As someone who worries about my character a lot, I'm concerned that moving so much has made me unable to make close friends, emotionally detached, and other things. In addition, I feel more resentful towards my parents because I'm somewhat sure that they could have prevented a few of the moves we've made. That's a different story, I guess.

To put it in perspective, on average I moved and enrolled at a new school each year since 4th/5th grade. Sometimes I stayed at one school for two years or more, and sometimes I only remained at a school for a few months.

Mental illness. I thought that probably people could buck up and fight through it and most people who talked about anxiety and depression who used drugs for it really shouldn't, because they could get over it on their own.

It ruined my personal relationships, because being afraid I was about to die all the time occupied my attention to the point that I was slow to respond and really acted weird. I was so nervous that I couldn't recall basic information, like my address. I had a whole bunch of physical symptoms. I was messy and barely holding it together, skipping class sometimes because I just didn't feel like I could handle leaving my apartment.

Started taking medication (although I was very skeptical of it). Within a couple of weeks I was a completely normal, functional human being. I had normal emotions, I cleaned, I was productive, I had conversations like a human being does. I will never again doubt that your brain chemistry being a bit screwy can really mess you up.
